defects.defectDesc: Writes `mergedResult._linterOverlap` ~280 lines BEFORE `mergedResult` is declared — a temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError that crashes the audit at runtime on that path.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags use-before-declaration / TDZ of mergedResult (assignment to a variable declared later in the same function scope)

defects.defectDesc: Judge pipeline had no tolerance for the model omitting rubric dimensions (and the egress redactor could corrupt dim names) — a strict schema rejects the pass with no corrective retry, so judgments fail on large prompts.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags that a schema-rejected judge response has no retry/corrective path (or that redaction can alter rubric-dimension tokens before the schema check) — LLM-boundary robustness

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/lib/store/debt.mjs:L30 + persona.mjs:L244 (raw JS arrays bound to jsonb columns)
defects.defectDesc: Raw JS arrays bound to jsonb columns via the pg driver — binds as a Postgres ARRAY literal → 22P02 for non-empty content and a SILENT `{}` for empty (the supabase-js→pg migration dropped PostgREST's implicit JSON serialization).
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags raw array/object values bound to jsonb parameters without JSON.stringify under node-postgres (22P02 / silent-{} write corruption)

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/brainstorm-round.mjs (arm-eval capture trigger — `envelope.round === 1` gate, as introduced)
defects.defectDesc: Off-by-one: the deterministic arm-eval capture trigger gated on `envelope.round === 1` ("first round only"), but the session ledger's `appendSession` numbers a session's FIRST round 0, not 1 — so a fresh brainstorm session could NEVER fire capture (only a `--continue-from` second round, numbered 1, would). Field-found by the wine-cellar-app verification run: no dispatch log line, no new arm_eval_sessions row.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags the mismatch between the trigger's 1-based round check and the ledger's 0-based round numbering (an off-by-one that silently disables the intended first-round-only behavior)

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/openai-audit.mjs (runMultiPassCodeAudit — `subjectFiles` declared inside the A1 guard block, as introduced)
defects.defectDesc: `subjectFiles` was declared with `const` inside the block-scoped A1 subject-file guard (`{ const subjectFiles = ...; ... }`), but a later call site far below in the same function — the model-A/B generation shadow's `buildRedactedAuditContext([...subjectFiles])` — referenced the same identifier outside that block. Dormant (best-effort-contained, so the baseline audit was unaffected) until the shadow harness was first enabled, at which point it threw a ReferenceError on every invocation — a crash bug, matching KD-001/KD-002's severity class.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags a block-scoped `const`/`let` binding referenced outside its enclosing block by a later call site in the same function (undefined-binding/ReferenceError crash risk that a happy-path test run would not exercise)

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/lib/nav/verify.mjs (discoverExpandTriggers — no visibility pre-filter, as introduced)
defects.defectDesc: `discoverExpandTriggers` selected activation triggers (e.g. a hamburger menu button) without filtering for visibility — a breakpoint-hidden trigger (`display:none` on desktop for a mobile-only hamburger) was still selected and clicked, wasting a 1000ms click-timeout plus an 'element is not visible' noise warning per state, since a `display:none`/0-size element can never actually be clicked.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags that an element-discovery routine selects DOM elements for interaction without a visibility/actionability check first (wasted timeout + noise on an unclickable target)

defects.defectDesc: The gap-challenge LLM call hardcoded a 3000-token output budget, sized against a 2-file smoke test. A real invariant-rich file set (a dozen modules) produces enough gap-assessment candidates to overflow that budget, yielding a length-truncated, unusable response — the caller had no signal that the response was cut off rather than complete.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags a hardcoded LLM output-token budget sized against a small test fixture rather than realistic input volume, with no truncation-detection or budget-scaling for larger inputs

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/check-skill-updates.mjs (managed-file path resolution — path.resolve(f.path) fallback, as introduced)
defects.defectDesc: For managed-file paths not matching a special-cased prefix list (.github/, .agents/, .audit-loop/), the fallback resolved the path via `path.resolve(f.path)` — relative to the process's current working directory — instead of the repo root. Running the check from any directory other than the repo root silently resolved managed files to the wrong absolute paths.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags a CWD-relative path fallback for what should be a repo-root-relative path resolution (invocation-directory-dependent bug, not caught by tests that always run from repo root)

defects.defectDesc: Rating badges rendered via innerHTML template interpolation of UNTRUSTED merchant-page data (r.source/r.score/r.range/r.scale) — a DOM-XSS vector in the extension popup.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags innerHTML (or equivalent HTML interpolation) of untrusted/external data in the popup rendering — XSS; remediation is DOM nodes/textContent

defects.evidenceHunk: src/routes/ratings.js (GET /api/ratings/logs handler as introduced — no admin guard, raw log lines + log path returned)
defects.defectDesc: Diagnostics endpoint GET /logs had NO admin guard — any authenticated user could read raw, unredacted server log lines plus the filesystem path (info-leak; secrets in logs exposed).
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags the unguarded diagnostics/log endpoint (missing authorization tier) and/or returning raw unredacted logs + server paths to callers

defects.defectDesc: Init race: on plugin load, a vault re-index can enqueue chunks BEFORE the async embedding service finishes initializing — drainOnce saw a null service and permanently dropped all pending chunks instead of waiting (data loss on every cold start with a large vault).
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags the race between queue consumption and async service initialization (null service treated as permanent failure → dropped work), needs bounded wait/retry

defects.defectDesc: Rename path calls `this.app.vault.getFileByPath(...)` — a method that does NOT exist on Obsidian's Vault API (the correct one is getAbstractFileByPath, used elsewhere in the same file) → guaranteed TypeError at runtime when renaming.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags the call to a non-existent API method (getFileByPath vs getAbstractFileByPath) — inconsistent with the same file's other call sites; runtime TypeError
defects.invalidatedReason: Premise contradicted by the real Obsidian API: Vault.getFileByPath(path: string): TFile | null IS a documented public method (obsidian.d.ts:6386, @since 1.5.7). Found + independently verified 2026-07-09 during the solo-control blind adjudication (a grader checked the typings directly). The only real residue is a possible minAppVersion compatibility gap, not a non-existent-method crash. Excluded from known-defect-recall denominators from this point on — do not count toward totals or match credit.

defects.defectDesc: The dependency auto-installer classifies @google/genai and @anthropic-ai/sdk as OPTIONAL_DEPS whose install failure is swallowed ("audit will degrade gracefully"), but the multi-model audit pipeline hard-imports both (Gemini auditor, Claude Opus fallback reviewer) — a consumer whose optional install fails gets a runtime import crash in the core audit flow, not graceful degradation.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags that dependencies the pipeline hard-requires at runtime (@google/genai and/or @anthropic-ai/sdk) are classified as optional with swallowed install failure — the required-vs-optional dependency classification does not match actual runtime imports

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/symbol-index/refresh.mjs:L261-L310 (extract/summarise/embed spawn call sites — cwd-relative script paths)
defects.defectDesc: The extract→summarise→embed pipeline spawns its sibling scripts via cwd-relative string paths (scripts/symbol-index/extract.mjs etc.) that only exist in the source-repo layout; in a consumer repo the tooling is relocated under scripts/.claude-skills/, so every spawn is MODULE_NOT_FOUND and arch:refresh is silently dead in all consumers.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags that sibling pipeline scripts are spawned via cwd-relative path strings instead of resolving relative to the current module (import.meta.dirname / fileURLToPath), breaking when the tooling is relocated to the consumer layout or invoked from a different working directory
defects.provenanceNote: The cwd-relative path SHAPE predates this commit; the WS-LIVE refactor re-presented the spawn call sites as added lines (blame introducer, not historical origin). Entry validity rests on diff-visibility + the documented relocation contract, not on original authorship.

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/ux-lock-run.mjs (cmdSpec — report test-file paths resolved via normalizeSpecPath(t.file, repoRoot) instead of the report rootDir)
defects.defectDesc: Silent data loss in the new Playwright runner CLI: Playwright JSON report file paths are emitted relative to the report's rootDir (bare basenames for a nested testDir), but the spec matcher resolves them against the repo root — every reported test is dropped as an orphan and the requested spec silently records 0 tests / passed:false.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags that Playwright JSON report file paths are resolved against the wrong base directory (repo root instead of the report rootDir/testDir), so reported tests fail to match the requested spec and are silently orphaned / recorded as zero tests

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/cache-hitrate-check.mjs:L28 (bare dotenv/config import) + L37-L45 (HAS_SUPABASE source selection with silent local fallback)
defects.defectDesc: The new cloud-aware source selection gates on credential env vars loaded via bare dotenv/config, which reads only the cwd .env — in this project the DB credentials normally live in the shared ~/.audit-loop.env, so any run outside the one directory with a local .env silently selects the stale per-machine local log and falsely reports INSUFFICIENT_DATA even when the DB holds ample runs (a wrong-green: the check reports a confident conclusion without having read the authoritative source).
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags that the data-source auto-selection depends on env vars that may not be loaded in this invocation context (cwd-only .env loading vs the shared env file), causing a silent fallback to stale/empty local data that is indistinguishable from a genuine no-data state

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/lib/file-io.mjs:L255-L390 (extractPlanPaths Phase 2 — _extractPlanKeywords/_scanRepoFiles fuzzy discovery, no exclusion of the audit tooling's own files)
defects.defectDesc: The new fuzzy file-discovery fallback (_scanRepoFiles + keyword matching) scans ALL repo files with no exclusion of the audit tooling's own synced scripts — in consumer repos (where these scripts are synced in) plan keywords fuzzily match the audit infrastructure itself, so the auditors flag issues in the audit tool instead of the project code under review.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags that the fuzzy repo-file scan has no exclusion/denylist for the audit tooling's own files (self-inclusion of infrastructure into audit scope), polluting audit context in consumer repos where the tooling is synced in

defects.evidenceHunk: scripts/setup-postgres.mjs:L37 (REPO_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..') — assumes the source-repo layout) + the repo-relative BOOTSTRAP_SQL path
defects.defectDesc: The new setup CLI resolves the repo root as path.resolve(__dirname, '..'), which is only correct in the source-repo layout (scripts/ one level below root); under the consumer synced layout (scripts/.claude-skills/) it lands on scripts/, so --migrate fails with ENOENT on the migrations dir in every consumer repo, and compat-bootstrap.sql is resolved repo-relative instead of script-relative.
defects.expectedFindingRubric: flags that repo-root/path resolution assumes the source layout (__dirname one level below root) and breaks under the documented consumer relocation layout (scripts/.claude-skills/) — path resolution must be layout-aware or script-relative
